name: bm-r4-coupled-2d-epithelium
title: Coupled 2D epithelial sheet
question: Do the paper's confinement regimes survive explicit cell topology and heterogeneous growth in a spatial 2D epithelium?
hypothesis: A Tyssue 2D polygonal sheet with a BM traction/area law calibrated from R2 reproduces R1's confinement response in the homogeneous limit, and explicit topology, cell division and varying cortical tensions introduce spatial force/area heterogeneity without destroying the regime structure.
objective: Build a Tyssue 2D sheet with a BM response calibrated from R2 (traction/area law, height via an explicit volume/prism relation); include a reference homogeneous case, cell division and varying cortical tensions; compare the confinement response to R1 and quantify topology sensitivity.
description:
The first spatial model (plan section 3, 2D planar level). A Tyssue polygonal sheet carries
a BM traction/area law calibrated from the R2 network rheology; cell height is inferred
through an explicit volume/prism relation. A homogeneous reference case must reproduce R1;
heterogeneous growth, division and cortical-tension variation then test whether the
confinement phase diagram is robust to explicit topology. Effective constitutive BM and
explicit LAMMPS BM are interchangeable alternatives here, not additive forces.

expected_behavior.name: confinement-robust-to-topology
expected_behavior.observable: confinement response vs R1; spatial force/area heterogeneity
expected_behavior.rationale: The homogeneous case must match R1; the regimes must survive explicit topology for P2 to advance.

baseline.name: bm-r4-coupled-2d-epithelium
baseline.note: A 2D epithelial sheet with explicit cell height, relaxed against a basement-membrane area law. It is the spatial counterpart of the homogeneous tissue model, so the confinement response can be read cell by cell rather than for one average cell.
